seoTitle: How to Add a Hyperlink in Jotform Easily
metaDescription: Learn how to insert a clickable hyperlink into a Jotform form in 2026 using the Paragraph element's rich text editor to link out cleanly.
intro: Linking out to terms and conditions, a product portfolio, or a downloadable resource is a common form need, and Jotform handles it through the Paragraph element's rich text editor. This guide covers adding that element, inserting your link, and setting it to open in a new tab without disrupting your form's design.

steps.heading: Add a Paragraph element
steps.body: Open the Form Elements sidebar and drag the Paragraph element block into your layout.

steps.heading: Open the rich text editor
steps.body: Double-click the paragraph canvas to activate the text editor toolbar.

steps.heading: Highlight your text and insert the link
steps.body: Select the display text you want clickable, then click the Insert Link tool in the toolbar.

steps.heading: Paste the URL and set the target
steps.body: Paste the destination URL and change the target property so the link opens in a new browser tab.

steps.heading: Save and test the link
steps.body: Save your changes, then refresh the preview window to confirm the hyperlink works and displays correctly on mobile.

faq.question: Can I style the hyperlink to match my form's color scheme?
faq.answer: Yes, the rich text editor lets you apply inline styling to your linked text so it matches your form's overall brand colors.

faq.question: Will the hyperlink open in the same window by default?
faq.answer: By default it may open in the same window, so it's worth explicitly setting the target property to a new tab if you don't want users to lose their form progress.

faq.question: Can I link to a downloadable file instead of a webpage?
faq.answer: Yes, as long as you have a direct URL to the file, you can paste it into the link field the same way as any other web link.

faq.question: Is there a limit to how many hyperlinks I can add to one form?
faq.answer: There's no strict limit, but adding too many links inside a single Paragraph element can clutter the form's design and confuse respondents.
